Felix uses a 12-inch Dobsonian as his primary scope and prefers red LED headlamps so his night vision stays intact. He always packs a thermos of espresso, a wool blanket, and a little box of sliced Swiss cheese for snack breaks between alignments. Felix refuses to use a phone for star charts during observing sessions and keeps hand-annotated star maps in a leather binder instead. He volunteers with a local dark-sky advocacy group and installs shielded fixtures for neighbors on weekend afternoons. Felix calibrates his mirrors with a laser collimator and keeps an old laser pointer stashed in the observatory drawer. He records naked-eye limiting magnitude and sky transparency in a logbook after every session and will only call a night 'worth it' if he can see the Andromeda arm faintly without a finder. He prefers high-elevation sites and will cancel if the forecast shows low transparency, no matter how clear the horizon looks. On rare clear winter nights he teaches newcomers to polar-align using only the Big Dipper.
